facts: Learned confidence measures gain increasing importance for outlier removal and quality improvement in stereo vision.
Acquiring the necessary training data is typically a tedious and time consuming task.
The acquisition of the necessary training data involves manual interaction.
The acquisition of the necessary training data involves active sensing devices.
The acquisition of the necessary training data involves synthetic scenes.
The authors propose a new, flexible, and scalable way for generating training data that only requires a set of stereo images as input.
The proposed way for generating training data is flexible.
The proposed way for generating training data is scalable.
The proposed way for generating training data only requires a set of stereo images as input.
The key idea of the approach is to use different view points.
The approach reasons about contradictions and consistencies between multiple depth maps.
The multiple depth maps are generated with the same stereo algorithm.
The approach enables the generation of a huge amount of training data in a fully automated manner.
The authors demonstrate the potential of the approach.

The authors boost the performance of three learned confidence measures on the KITTI2012 dataset by simply training them on a vast amount of automatically generated training data rather than a limited amount of laser ground truth data.
